# ============================================================
# New analyses (2026-07 session): polarity synthesis, TAM-1 diagnosis,
# VGP diagnosis, age model + Purussaurus fossil anchor
# ============================================================
These cells reproduce, from repo-relative paths, the work added in July 2026:
1. **Corrected polarity synthesis** from the despiked 300–1000 PCA fits.
2. **TAM Group 1 diagnosis** — why its polarity is not recoverable.
3. **VGP diagnosis** — why VGPs do not cluster at the poles (unoriented + shallow).
4. **Age model + Purussaurus fossil bracket** and multi-GPTS comparison.

Run top-to-bottom. Standalone scripts also live in `polarity_synthesis/` and
`age_model_assessment/`.

## 2 — TAM Group 1 (TAM 1/2/3B): polarity NOT recoverable
Group 1 was measured at only **two steps** (NRM + one ~12.5 mT / 125 Oe step), so
there is no high-coercivity series to fit a ChRM to (PCA over 300–1000 is degenerate,
MAD = 0). The two-step directions are steep and scattered = coring overprint. The cell
below shows this directly from the raw `.DAT`.

raw="OSU_uchannel_magnetometer_NRM_data/TAM_1_2_3B_NRM_01192026.DAT"
rows=[r.rstrip("\n").split("\t") for r in open(raw)]; h=rows[0]
iI,iR,iP=h.index("Inclination: Unrotated"),h.index("Run #"),h.index("Position")
def grab(run): return np.array([[float(r[iP]),float(r[iI])] for r in rows[1:] if r[iR]==run and _num(r[iP]) and _num(r[iI])])
def _num(x):
    try: float(x); return True
    except: return False
runs=sorted(set(r[iR] for r in rows[1:] if r[iR]))
print("runs (demag steps) in TAM_1_2_3B:",runs," -> only NRM + one AF step")
for run in runs:
    a=grab(run); ai=a[a[:,0]>=0]
    print(f"  run {run}: n={len(ai)} incl median={np.median(ai[:,1]):+.1f} "
          f"IQR[{np.percentile(ai[:,1],25):+.1f},{np.percentile(ai[:,1],75):+.1f}]")
print("Verdict: no ChRM isolable -> Group 1 EXCLUDED; TAM top normal not preserved.")

## 3 — Why VGPs do NOT cluster at the poles (diagnosis)
The cores are azimuthally **unoriented**, yet one fixed azimuth/declination was applied
per multi-sub-core group. At this **shallow** (~4°S) inclination, VGP latitude is
hypersensitive to the (unknown) declination — so VGPs smear across all latitudes.
VGPs are therefore **not** a valid polarity/QC tool here; use inclination sign.

def vgp_lat(site_lat,inc,dec):
    slat,I,D=np.radians(site_lat),np.radians(inc),np.radians(dec)
    p=np.arctan2(2.0,np.tan(I))
    return np.degrees(np.arcsin(np.sin(slat)*np.cos(p)+np.cos(slat)*np.sin(p)*np.cos(D)))
print("VGP latitude vs (unknown) declination at 4S:")
print(" shallow normal inc=-8:", [f"D={D}:{vgp_lat(-3.4,-8,D):+.0f}" for D in (0,45,90,135,180)])
print(" steep       inc=-60:", [f"D={D}:{vgp_lat(-3.4,-60,D):+.0f}" for D in (0,45,90,135,180)])
print("-> shallow incl: VGP_lat swings +89..-83 as dec varies (unoriented => scatter).")

## 4 — Age model: Purussaurus + palynology bracket, multi-GPTS
Palynology (T15/T16) sets a **floor** (>12.7 Ma); *Purussaurus* genus FAD sets a
**ceiling** (<~13.8 Ma). Together: ~12.7–13.8 Ma. SC's N–R–N thickness ratio favors
**C5AAr–C5ABr** (~13.2–13.7 Ma). GTS2020 = GTS2012 here; CK95 is ~50–100 kyr younger.

NORM={"C5An.1n":(12.049,12.174),"C5An.2n":(12.272,12.474),"C5Ar.1n":(12.735,12.770),
 "C5Ar.2n":(12.829,12.887),"C5AAn":(13.032,13.183),"C5ABn":(13.363,13.608),
 "C5ACn":(13.739,14.070),"C5ADn":(14.163,14.609)}
PAL_FLOOR,PURU_CEIL=12.7,13.8
fig,ax=plt.subplots(figsize=(4.5,7)); lo,hi=11.9,14.7
for nm,(t,b) in NORM.items():
    ax.axhspan(t,b,xmin=0,xmax=0.25,color="k"); ax.text(-0.02,(t+b)/2,nm,ha="right",va="center",fontsize=7)
ax.axhspan(PAL_FLOOR,hi,xmin=0.35,xmax=0.5,color="#c0392b",alpha=.2); ax.axhline(PAL_FLOOR,0.35,0.5,color="#c0392b",lw=2)
ax.axhspan(lo,PURU_CEIL,xmin=0.55,xmax=0.7,color="#27ae60",alpha=.2); ax.axhline(PURU_CEIL,0.55,0.7,color="#1e8449",lw=2)
ax.axhspan(PAL_FLOOR,PURU_CEIL,xmin=0.78,xmax=0.93,color="#f1c40f",alpha=.35)
ax.text(0.855,(PAL_FLOOR+PURU_CEIL)/2,"ALLOWED\n12.7-13.8 Ma",ha="center",va="center",fontsize=7,rotation=90)
ax.text(0.42,PAL_FLOOR-0.05,"palyno floor\n>12.7 Ma",color="#c0392b",fontsize=7,ha="center",va="top")
ax.text(0.62,PURU_CEIL+0.05,"Purussaurus\nceiling <13.8 Ma",color="#1e8449",fontsize=7,ha="center",va="bottom")
ax.set_ylim(hi,lo); ax.set_xlim(-0.1,1); ax.set_xticks([]); ax.set_ylabel("Age (Ma)")
ax.set_title("Fossil + palyno bracket the section"); plt.tight_layout(); plt.show()

### Findings summary (2026-07)
- **Polarity:** TAM = R–N (top normal lost); SC = N–R–N–N–N; one shared reversal.
- **TAM Group 1:** unrecoverable (only NRM + 12.5 mT) — needs re-measurement.
- **VGPs:** scatter is an unoriented + shallow-inclination artifact, not a data fault.
- **Age:** *Purussaurus* (ceiling ≤13.8 Ma) + palyno (floor ≥12.7 Ma) → 12.7–13.8 Ma;
  SC pattern favors C5AAr–C5ABr (~13.2–13.7 Ma). Species ID of the fossil is the tiebreaker.
